strategies.name: Fused Coupling with Batched All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Pre-compute all coupling operations locally and batch them into a single buffer structure, then issue all-reduces on strategically arranged memory views to reduce dispatch overhead. Dispatch count = 8 all-reduces but with optimized payload layout to enable back-to-back pipelining. Reduces memory allocation overhead by reusing buffers across stages.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction Tree
strategies.desc: Exploit the 224 = 28 nodes × 8 devices structure by performing intra-node reductions first (8-way within each node), then inter-node reductions (28-way across nodes), applying bidiagonal coupling at appropriate hierarchical levels. Dispatch count = 16 collectives (8 stages × 2 levels). Trades increased dispatch count for reduced per-dispatch latency on smaller communication groups.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Pipeline
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pair, allowing local bidiagonal coupling to happen on scattered shards between phases. Dispatch count = 16 collectives (8 stages × 2 primitives). Reduces bandwidth requirements by limiting full-vector communication, trading dispatch count for smaller per-rank payloads.

strategies.name: Overlapped Computation with Async Collectives
strategies.desc:
Issue all-reduce operations asynchronously and overlap the bidiagonal coupling/decoupling computation of stage N with the communication of stage N-1 using non-blocking collectives. Dispatch count = 8 all-reduces but with wait barriers strategically placed. Hides computation latency within communication latency, trading code complexity for potential wall-clock speedup.
